results.reply: A heads-up before the specifics: this assistant holds no curated, verified data for Nauru and Uzbekistan - they are outside the knowledge base this covers. Everything below on them came from a live web search this turn instead, so treat it as unconfirmed and check it yourself before relying on it. Based on your current situation in Thailand, I recommend heading to Uzbekistan for September. It's significantly more budget-friendly, aligning well with your shoestring budget of street food and dorms. You can expect a daily budget of about $20 to $30 USD, with dorm accommodations around $5-10 and meals starting as low as $1-2 (live-sourced/unconfirmed from [source](https://thepartyingtraveler.com/2026/03/25/backpacker-travel-guide-uzbekistan)). On the other hand, Nauru may set you back around $90 to $130 USD daily, with limited accommodation options starting at $60-80 (live-sourced/unconfirmed from [source](https://www.annaroundtheworld.com/blog/everything-you-need-to-know-about-nauru)). Given your slow travel pace and preference for cost-effective options, Uzbekistan seems like the better fit right now.

results.message: Getting to Laos or Malaysia from here - is it worth going overland?
results.reply: I recommend going to Laos over Malaysia due to its cheaper travel experience and budget-friendly options, which fit your shoestring budget and slow travel pace. Expect to spend between **$18-25** per day. You can take a sleeper train from Bangkok to Nong Khai, crossing the Friendship Bridge to Vientiane in about **12 hours** for around **$30-45**. This aligns with your interest in rivers, as traveling on the Mekong slow boat from Huay Xai to Luang Prabang is a classic experience costing about **$35**. You're currently in Thailand and looking for cost-effective routes, so Laos is the best option right now.

backpacker_notes: Mekong slow boat from Huay Xai to Luang Prabang for about $35.
Sleeper train from Bangkok to Nong Khai takes about 12 hours for $30-45.
Expect to spend $18-25 per day in Laos.
Be cautious of unexploded ordnance in eastern regions.
Bus from Bangkok to Butterworth takes about 20 hours for $30-50.
Complete the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card online for free before arriving.
Ensure you use reputable transport services for safety.
